page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and contains a 33 MB L3 cache. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves average tier results in single-core CPU stress tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core assessments. However, multi-core processing is limited, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the lower performance quartiles. Memory bandwidth is also restricted, registering weak read and write speeds under large-block testing, which impacts data-intensive operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.u1-c1m2.xlarge offers an entry-level dedicated compute profile with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This resource density makes it a viable option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without demanding high memory capacity or local storage IOPS. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, and small-scale application hosting where multi-core scaling and high memory throughput are not critical.
